unit.why: A short anecdote: a great scholar asks the Seer of Lublin why crowds come to him rather than to the scholar, and the Seer answers with humility and a witty reversal.

stories.start_quote: פ״א שאל רב גאון אחד את הרבי מלובלין
stories.summary_en: A great Torah scholar asks the Seer of Lublin why many Jews flock to him and not to the scholar, who is more learned; the Seer humbly replies that he himself wonders at it, and that perhaps people come to him because he knows his own low worth, and they leave the scholar because the scholar wonders why they do not come.

quotes: כי אנכי ידעתי ערכי השפל מי אנכי ומה אנכי
וידעתי ערכי כי איני ראוי לאותו איצטלא
tags.why: The Seer's self-effacement is the point of the answer

quotes: הלא אנכי ת"ח גדול ומופלג בתורה מאד יותר מרום כבודו
tags.why: The scholar's self-regard is contrasted with the Seer's humility
The anecdote illustrates the tzaddik's humility
